verdict: ConocoPhillips earned $4.0B as higher oil and gas prices — an average realized price of $61.40 per barrel of oil equivalent, up 32% — lifted revenue 29% to $20.1B, and it raised its dividend 11%.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $20.1B in total revenues and other income, vs $15.5B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $1.38 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $3.27

kpis.label: Production
kpis.note: Thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day — down 97 from a year ago

kpis.label: Returned to shareholders
kpis.note: $2.4B of share buybacks plus $1.0B of dividends in the quarter

segments.name: Sales & other operating revenues
segments.note: Selling the oil and gas the company produces — the realized price averaged $61.40 per barrel of oil equivalent, up 32% from $46.44 a year ago, more than offsetting lower volumes.

segments.name: Equity in earnings of affiliates
segments.note: ConocoPhillips' share of profit from partnerships and jointly owned operations it does not fully control.

segments.name: Other income
segments.note: Smaller income items outside direct oil and gas sales.

segments.name: Gain on dispositions
segments.note: Profit on selling assets — the company also received $1.6B of cash proceeds from selling noncore assets in the quarter.

opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of wells and fields over the oil and gas they produce — the biggest running cost after buying commodities.

opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.note: The growing present value of future site-restoration (asset retirement) obligations as time passes.

takeaways.title: Prices, not volumes, drove the quarter
takeaways.text: The average realized price rose 32% to $61.40 per barrel of oil equivalent while production fell 97 MBOED to 2,302 MBOED — after closed sales and purchases, output was down 2%, with Middle East conflict effects in Qatar and higher Canadian royalties partly offsetting Lower 48 growth.

takeaways.title: Cash flow funded big returns
takeaways.text: Cash from operations was $7.2B. ConocoPhillips spent $3.1B on capital projects and returned $3.4B to shareholders — $2.4B of buybacks and $1.0B of dividends — staying on track to return 45% of operating cash flow in 2026. The quarterly dividend was raised 11% to $0.93 a share.

takeaways.title: Willow is the long bet
takeaways.text: The Willow project in Alaska passed 75% completion on module fabrication and stays on track for first oil in early 2029. The company also grew its commercial LNG offtake portfolio to 13 million tonnes per year and ended the quarter with $10.4B of cash and short-term investments.

oneTimers: GAAP earnings of $4.0B were slightly above adjusted earnings of $3.9B ($3.27 a share) — the special items the company adjusts for primarily reflect the reversal of a tax reserve.
otherDetail: Other expense of $163M, net: $142M of interest and debt expense, a $10M foreign-currency transaction loss and $11M of other expenses.
footerNote: ConocoPhillips reports total revenues and other income of $20,057M, used as revenue here: its equity earnings, disposition gains and other income are reported above that total, so they are shown as revenue sources. Depreciation, depletion and amortization ($3,005M) is a large, non-cash cost of producing oil and gas and is shown with operating expenses in this mapping; the direct-cost block is purchased commodities ($7,423M) plus production and operating expenses ($2,440M).
